text:
maria: ACME asked for an explicit "grace lane" for short spikes — they want traffic to be accepted even when quota is near exhaustion, with a clear fallback sequence and billing transparency. Can we scope this for Q4?

dan: Curious what product means by "short" — seconds, tens of seconds? Need to define SLOs for accepted-but-demoted calls. Also say whether this is tenant-level only or pool-level.

krish: My reading: aim for <10s unthrottled for burst requests under N tokens. Proposed operator: grace_lane = allow extra concurrency for requests with token_estimate <= 1024 for up to M seconds while draining heavier requests. After M window, apply demotion sequence.

krish: Quick config example (for RFC):
```yaml
reserved_pool:
  name: acme-prod
  quota:
    max_concurrent: 120
    grace_lane:
      enabled: true
      burst_window_s: 12
      token_threshold: 1024
      demotion_order:
        - redwood-3b-quant
        - redwood-1b
        - reject
      telemetry_tags: ["grace_lane", "demotion_reason"]
```

olivia: Love the small-window approach. From go-to-market: launch criteria we need: 1) e2e perf test showing p95 latency change <200ms for demoted requests, 2) cost delta report (projected) + billing attribution per-demotion, 3) customer-facing docs explaining behavior and how to opt-out.

billing-bot: billing: please ensure demoted-model usage emits `demoted_model_usage` event with fields: tenant_id, original_model, demoted_model, token_count, billed_model.

maria: Ops asks: ensure demotion is scoped to tenant's reserved pool only. If pool saturated, spill to regional elastic lane (not cross-tenant). Also need a circuit-breaker metric to stop demotions if downstream latency climbs.

dan: Implementation notes: prefer in-runtime demotion (same worker swaps model weights) vs routing to a different pool to avoid client-side latency hops. But weight-swap has memory constraints. We'll need memory profiling and an autoscale rule for prewarm when grace_lane enabled.

krish: Ownership checklist draft:
- API: tenant-level opt-in flag `grace_lane_v1`
- Console: show grace_lane usage and demotion history per-tenant
- Telemetry: `demotion_rate`, `grace_lane_accepts`, `avg_demoted_latency` + alert if demotion_rate > 1% for 15m
- Billing: emit demoted_model_usage events + nightly reconciliation job
- Ops: prewarm policy: when tenant enables grace_lane, allocate 10% prewarm buffer in pool for quantized variants
- Pilot: run with ACME and 2 internal tenants for 2 weeks

olivia: Prioritization: this should be a medium-high roadmap item tied to Dedicated-commit level customers. If we take on ACME pilot, move to top of the backlog for the next sprint.

maria: Legal wants simple phrasing: "grace_lane may use lower-capacity model variants on a best-effort basis; in rare cases, requests may be rejected." Dan, can you write proposed contract language?

dan: I can draft a short paragraph. Also will add a risk note about cross-pool contagion and mitigation (prewarm + pool-local demotion only).

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Feature branch `grace_lane_v1` created. Canary schedule: dry-run to prod-canary on 2024-11-06T09:00Z.

krish: Next steps: I'll write RFC with config schema, failure modes, and memory prewarm numbers. Maria please coordinate ACME legal/product. Olivia will prepare launch acceptance template and cost thresholds. Dan to add contract blurb + ops runbook. Meeting Friday 11am to triage pilot scope. :rocket:

maria: Thanks team — adding to Friday agenda and filing RFC link when ready.
